nodes.name: One-step solvothermal synthesis of x-MO
nodes.procedure: The x-MO/CdS heterostructures were synthesized using one-step solvothermal method. The Ov concentration in MoO3-x can be precisely controlled by varying the amount of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), which has strong oxidizing and reducing ability. With 3, 11, and 15 mL of H2O2 addition, MoO3-x with poor, rich, and moderate Ov concentrations were obtained. The samples were denoted as P-MO, R-MO, and M-MO, respectively.
nodes.source_text: The x-MO/CdS heterostructures were synthesized using one-step solvothermal method. The Ov concentration in MoO3-x can be precisely controlled by varying the amount of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)... The samples were denoted as P-MO, R-MO, and M-MO, respectively.

nodes.name: Synthesis of CdS nanorods
nodes.procedure: Hexagonal CdS nanorods with high crystallinity were successfully synthesized.
nodes.source_text: The XRD pattern in Fig. 2a and the TEM images with distinct lattice stripes in Fig. S9 indicate that hexagonal CdS nanorods with high crystallinity were successfully synthesized.

nodes.name: Electrostatic self-assembly of x-MO/CdS heterojunctions
nodes.procedure: To confirm the feasibility of the proposed strategy for regulating photocatalytic activity, x-MO was coupled with CdS nanorod to construct an x-MO/CdS heterojunction photocatalyst via electrostatic self-assembly. The R-MO content was optimized at 15 % (Fig. S17).

nodes.characterization_summary: P-MO, R-MO and M-MO show diffraction peaks at 12.47°, 23.50°, 25.37°, 26.99°, 33.9°, and 38.38° assigned to (020), (110), (040), (021), (111), and (060) planes of orthorhombic MoO3-x (JCPDS 70-0615).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern in Fig. 1a shows diffraction peaks at 12.47°, 23.50°, 25.37°, 26.99°, 33.9°, and 38.38°, which are assigned to the (020), (110), (040), (021), (111), and (060) planes of orthorhombic MoO3-x...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images of R-MO display nanosheet morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM (Fig. 1b) and HRTEM (Fig. 1c) images display discontinuous lattice stripes, indicative of crystal defects in x-MO.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows R-MO with lattice spacing of 0.351 nm corresponding to (040) plane and discontinuous lattice stripes indicating crystal defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM (Fig. 1b) and HRTEM (Fig. 1c) images display discontinuous lattice stripes, indicative of crystal defects in x-MO.

nodes.characterization_summary: R-MO displays higher EPR signal intensity at g=2.001 compared to P-MO and M-MO, confirming higher oxygen vacancy concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: R-MO displayed a relatively higher EPR signal intensity at g=2.001 compared to the other samples, confirming that more electrons were trapped at Ov in the MO nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution O 1s XPS shows peaks at 530.23 eV (lattice oxygen), 531.25 eV (defect oxygen Ov), 532.63 eV (adsorbed oxygen) with Ov ratio 27.15% in R-MO (vs 23.16% P-MO, 24.46% M-MO). Mo 3d XPS shows Mo6+ reduced to Mo5+ in R-MO/CdS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectrum of O 1s in Fig. 1e further supports the high OV concentration in R-MO... the relative ratio of Ov in R-MO (Ov/(OL+Ov+OA)=27.15%) is higher than that of P-MO (23.16%) and M-MO (24.46%)... due to the large number of Ov in x-MO, Mo6+ is reduced to low-valence Mo5+, as evidenced by the high-resolution XPS spectrum of the Mo 3d spectrum in Fig. 1f.

nodes.characterization_summary: x-MO nanosheets show intrinsic absorption edge ~400 nm with R-MO exhibiting strongest tailing absorption due to higher Ov concentration. Bandgaps: P-MO 2.58 eV, R-MO 2.27 eV, M-MO 2.35 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the UV–vis–NIR absorption spectra in Fig. 1g, the x-MO nanosheets exhibit intrinsic absorption edges around 400 nm... From the corresponding Tauc plots for x-MO... the band gap (Eg) of x-MO (2.58, 2.27, and 2.35 eV for P-MO, R-MO, and M-MO, respectively)...

nodes.characterization_summary: R-MO shows superior photothermal conversion: surface temperature reaches 120.8°C (visible), 54.3°C (NIR), higher than P-MO and M-MO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Under visible light irradiation (420–780 nm), the surface temperatures of P-MO, R-MO, and M-MO increased to 113.9, 120.8, and 117.0 °C... the surface temperature of R-MO reached 54.3 and 120.8 °C under NIR light (Fig. S4) and full-spectrum irradiation...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows CdS nanorods wrapped around R-MO nanosheets surface in R-MO/CdS heterojunction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM (Fig. 2b) and TEM (Fig. 2c) images show that the CdS nanorods were wrapped around the surface of the R-MO nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF image and elemental mappings confirm R-MO nanosheets wrapped in CdS nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) image of the R-MO/CdS heterojunction and the corresponding elemental mappings in Fig. S10 confirm that the R-MO nanosheets were wrapped in CdS nanorods.

nodes.characterization_summary: All x-MO samples show positive slopes confirming n-type semiconductor behavior. R-MO has smallest slope yielding highest carrier density ND=2.0×10^25 cm^-3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The positive slopes of the linear regions indicate that x-MO is a typical n-type semiconductor... The calculated ND for R-MO is 2.0×10^25/cm3, much higher than that of M-MO (1.28×10^25/cm3) and P-MO (1.48×10^25/cm3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Work functions: CdS 3.75 eV, P-MO 3.87 eV, M-MO 4.19 eV, R-MO 4.34 eV. Fermi levels: CdS -0.69 V, P-MO -0.57 V, M-MO -0.25 V, R-MO -0.1 V vs NHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) was further performed... the work function (Φ) can be estimated to be 3.75, 3.87, 4.19, and 4.34 eV for CdS, P-MO, M-MO, and R-MO, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: R-MO/CdS shows significantly smaller EIS semicircle radius indicating enhanced charge separation efficiency.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EIS semicircle radius of R-MO/CdS was significantly smaller than that of the other samples (Fig. 4f), indicating enhanced charge separation efficiency.

nodes.characterization_summary: x-MO/CdS heterojunctions show typical IV isotherms with H3 hysteresis loops indicating mesoporous structure with higher BET surface areas than CdS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the BET surface areas of the samples were determined through adsorption-desorption isotherms under an N2 atmosphere in Fig. S26. The typical IV curves, showing H3 hysteresis loops, suggest a mesoporous structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: R-MO/CdS exhibits highest surface photovoltage and photocurrent density due to abundant Ov.
nodes.evidence_snippet: R-MO/CdS exhibited the highest surface photocurrent density and photovoltage due to the present of abundant Ov.

nodes.characterization_summary: R-MO/CdS shows highest zeta potential value consistent with enhanced IEF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: R-MO/CdS has a notably higher zeta potential value than the other samples, consistent with the SPV results.

nodes.characterization_summary: R-MO/CdS shows decreased PL intensity indicating reduced charge recombination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the decreased PL intensity of R-MO/CdS indicates significantly reduced charge recombination (Fig. 4g).

nodes.characterization_summary: R-MO/CdS charge carrier lifetime 14.79 ns vs CdS 10.37 ns, indicating prolonged lifetime due to S-scheme transfer and Ov trapping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with CdS (10.37 ns), R-MO/CdS (14.79 ns) exhibits a prolonged lifetime due to the S-scheme charge transfer and Ov acting as electron trap centers...

nodes.characterization_summary: R-MO/CdS shows lower overpotential η10 and Tafel slope than CdS and R-MO, indicating improved HER energy barrier and kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: LSV plots in Fig. 4i show that R-MO/CdS has a much lower overpotential η10 and Tafel slope than CdS and R-MO, indicating that the H2 evolution reaction energy barrier and kinetics were remarkably improved.
